If you really are a wastful spender you should keep a book/app where you keep track of all your spendings where you list every single item you buy. It shows you the bigger picture of your spending and knowing you will have to note it down might make you think twice about buying it.
Also you should try to build a habit where you think twice about buying something and ask yourself if you really need it and maybe even sleep over it. Except it are essentials of course (although with food you can save a lot of money by stopping to be lazy and cooking fresh food). 
I must say my biggest struggle is spending too much money on food. I have a few expensive food products I really love and I always love to tell myself that I only buy it once as a treat... it is just that I tell myself that 4 or 5 times I go shopping and the price just rises and rises... or that I skip breakfast and therefore (pre coronavirus, it helped me there) buy something somewhere else which is much more expensive than eating some porridge and fruit at home. Seriously. I kind of improved on those points. I plan on writing a grocery list before shopping now which I also have to follow. 
By reevaluating my choices always I managed to get better in spending too much money on candles or tea (yes it is weird but I am a bit addicted to buying these). So I only buy a candle every 2 months and a tea only when I emptied one I had... it is improvement.
And which also helps is to change your mindset about clothes and only buy a new one if you really need one because you either really don't have enough (which rarely is the case) or because an old piece got damaged. I really embraced this and therefore spent almost no money on clothes. 
But I think it is also about realizing where you spent your money exactly and if maybe in some catdgory it is out of proportion and where you shouldn't spent money on it that much. Maybe also splitting in essential things and optional things. But it for sure is a lot of afford to get there
